name: Park Hyatt Beijing
positioning: High-rise Park Hyatt in the Beijing Yintai Centre on Chang'an Avenue in the central business district, with its lobby on the 63rd floor
best_for: Travelers who want a high-floor base in Beijing's central business district
Guests who want a subway station and a shopping mall within easy reach

facts.text: The hotel is situated in Beijing's central business district.
The hotel sits within the Beijing Yintai Centre skyscraper on Chang'an Avenue.
The lobby is on the 63rd floor.
Guomao subway station is a one-minute walk from the front door.
China World Mall is connected to the hotel via underground passageways.
Each room has 300-thread-count linens, down duvets, a separate shower, a walk-in closet and a coffee machine.
Rooms have a centralized PM2.5 air purification system.
China Grill specialises in premium meat, fish and seafood.
At lunch and dinner, Dining Room serves Cantonese and Chaozhou-style dishes.
China Bar serves vintage wines and Champagnes by the glass, cocktails, whiskeys and Cognacs, with daily live entertainment.
Tian Spa draws on ancient Chinese wellness practices.
Breakfast includes Beijing specialties, each with a small sign explaining the dish's history.

highlights.text: At China Grill, diners sit beneath a Chinese lantern-style glass pyramid ceiling at the building's apex, with glass walls, trees and water features.
Park Hyatt Beijing was the first Park Hyatt to open in China.
In the rooms, one push on the doors reveals skyline views from the soaking tub or the shower.
Dining Room is a Chinese restaurant on the 63rd floor with panoramic city views.
Dining Room invites guest chefs from Hyatt hotels in other Chinese cities to bring regional flavors.

considerations.text: The hotel recommends local mapping apps such as Gaode Map or Baidu Map, as international mapping apps may not be accurate in mainland China.
Many sites are blocked in China, including Google and Gmail.
WhataHotel notes the business district location may lack a traditional cultural atmosphere.

sources.title: Conde Nast Traveler: Park Hyatt Beijing
